item.title: Japan ST Mark and Korea KC: Selling Toys into Japan and Korea
item.description: Japan and Korea both test toys for the same hazards as the EU and US — but neither accepts an EN71 or CPC report. What the ST Mark and KC confirmation actually require, who can apply, and how to plan the labels.

item.title: Pet Toy Export to the US: What Actually Applies
item.description: Pet toys are not covered by CPSIA, which surprises most buyers. Here is what does apply — FDA feed rules for edible chews, state chemical laws, Amazon documentation, and labeling.

item.title: TPR vs PU vs Silicone: Which Squishy Toy Material to Choose
item.description: TPR, PU foam and silicone squishy toys look similar but differ in cost, rebound, smell, tearing and compliance. A side-by-side comparison for buyers specifying material.

item.title: CPC Certificate for Amazon Toy Sellers: What Actually Gets Rejected
item.description: What a Children's Product Certificate must contain to clear Amazon and US customs, why most toy CPCs get rejected, and how to get one from a Chinese factory.

item.title: EN71, ASTM F963 and GPSR: Which Toy Certificate You Need Where
item.description: A country-by-country map of what a toy actually needs: EN71 for the EU, ASTM F963 and CPC for the US, plus the EU responsible person rule under GPSR that catches most importers.

item.title: Toy Safety Certifications Explained: CE, EN71, ASTM F963, GPSR
item.description: Everything B2B toy buyers need to know about global toy safety certifications. Which ones you need, how to get them, and avoiding costly compliance mistakes.
